title: Necklace, chain

altText: A Roman necklace made as a gold chain, a row of linked gold parts that could be worn around the neck.

context: A gold chain necklace made in the Roman world in the 1st century CE. Gold chains were a common form of Roman jewelry, and goldsmiths made them by joining many small links or elements into a flexible strand.

descriptions.k: This is a gold chain from ancient Rome. It is made of many little pieces linked together. People wore it around the neck. How do you think it moved when someone walked?
descriptions.g12: This gold necklace was made in ancient Rome about 2,000 years ago. It is a chain made of many small gold pieces joined together. The chain can bend and swing like a snake. Look closely at the links. How do you think a goldsmith made so many matching pieces?
descriptions.g35: A Roman goldsmith made this necklace as a chain of many small gold parts joined together. Because the parts link, the necklace bends and drapes around the neck. Look for how the pieces repeat. The pattern makes the necklace beautiful and flexible at once. How might someone have made so many matching parts by hand?
descriptions.g68: Roman gold chains were made by joining many small elements into a flexible strand, which required patience and precision. This necklace dates to the 1st century CE, when gold jewelry marked wealth and taste across the Roman world. Because it is a chain, its appeal comes from repetition and movement as much as from any single shape. How does repetition make a simple design rich, and why might Romans have valued such objects?
descriptions.g910: A gold chain necklace puts pattern, material, and movement at the center. Repeated links create rhythm, and gold's shine and weight make the strand feel luxurious. Unlike a pendant, the necklace has no single focal point, so its beauty depends on consistency and craftsmanship along its entire length. Consider how a flexible object that was made to move and catch light differs from a static sculpture. What does the choice of a chain suggest about Roman ideas of elegance?
descriptions.g1112: This Roman gold chain shows how a modest-looking form can embody technical skill and social display. The record gives limited information about its construction and wearer, so inferences about technique, status, or gender should be cautious. A chain is defined by repetition, flexibility, and movement, qualities that museum display largely freezes. Consider how the necklace's meaning changes between its function on a body in the 1st century CE and its role as a preserved object today, and what the absence of figural imagery reveals about luxury.

teacherNote.context: A Roman gold chain necklace of the 1st century CE. Gold jewelry was widely worn in the Roman Empire, and chains were a common way to display skill and wealth.
directions: Have students make a paper chain and discuss how repeating one small unit builds a larger pattern.
Compare this necklace with a modern chain: what has stayed the same and what has changed?
Discuss why gold, which does not rust, is found in museums from so long ago.
